title: Cross-service Release Windowing and Escalation Matrix for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define an operationally-safe, repeatable calendar and gating mechanism to coordinate parallel release trains across Runtime, Console, and Public API so we can reduce merge conflicts, avoid coupled rollbacks, and provide predictable windows for enterprise customers. Scope: Produce a canonical release window template, escalation matrix, gating checklist, and automation tasks for calendar enforcement. This ticket covers cross-service coordination (runtime engine changes, console UX updates, api contract bumps) and the communication/automation required to carry out coordinated launches.

Key stakeholders: PM (Diego Martinez), Runtime Eng Lead (Lena Chen), Console Eng Lead (Marcus O'Neill), API Platform Lead (Harpreet Singh), Release Manager (Olivia Park), SRE (Ethan Kim), Security (Rohit Verma), Design (Maya Lopez).

Deliverables: 1) Release window cadence doc (preferred windows, blackout periods for enterprise customers, region-aware scheduling). 2) Escalation matrix (triage owners, SLAs for critical failures, rollback vs patch decision tree). 3) Gating checklist per surface (automated test pass thresholds, perf SLO verification, DB migration readiness, feature flags & kill-switch validation, API contract checks). 4) Calendar automation: short scripts / webhooks to lock/unlock release windows in calendar, auto-post to #releases and to customer status page. 5) Runbook for cross-train canary and progressive rollout with measurable criteria.

Trade-offs and decisions to consider: - Synchronizing large runtime upgrades with small console/UI tweaks increases blast radius; prefer decoupled canary strategy with coordinated fallback policies. - Narrower release windows reduce coordination overhead but increase frequency of small releases; balance with team capacity. - Prefer policy of "runtime-first" for infra/compatibility breaking changes followed by console and API non-breaking deployments within the same train, unless an API contract bump mandates ordering.

Gating criteria (draft): - Runtime: non-regression perf tests (p95 latency < baseline + 10%), smoke at 10% traffic, KV cache integrity checks, zero silent failures after 1 hour. - API: contract tests green, backwards compatible flags set or explicit migration plan, docs published. - Console: E2E critical flows green, feature flags enabled in canary, no console-only breaking changes for enterprise tenants in same window.

Escalation matrix (high level): - T0 (sev0): runtime crash or data corruption => SRE page, full rollback within 30min unless mitigation fixes exist. - T1 (sev1): degraded latency above SLO for >15min => call with Runtime Eng Lead and Release Manager; consider traffic shed or degraded feature mode. - T2/T3: console visual regressions or doc errors => patch in next micro-release, not necessarily rollback.

Automation & calendar integration: integrate with Google Calendar (team calendars), Linear, and #releases Slack channel. Deliver small automation that: a) posts start/end of window; b) updates status in Linear for dependent tickets; c) prevents scheduling of new high-risk migrations in locked windows. Proposed repo: github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools (PR template and webhook).

Risks: - Cross-service dependencies not fully identified leading to blocked trains. - Insufficient observability on low-frequency outages during canary. - Enterprise customers in multiple regions require staggered windows which complicates automation.

Success metrics: - Reduce cross-train rollbacks by 60% vs Q1. - 90% of coordinated releases follow the gating checklist. - Time-to-decision for rollbacks <= 45 minutes on sev1/0 events.

Next steps: 1) Align stakeholders in release-design workshop (scheduled 2026-03-15). 2) Produce first draft of release window template and gating checklist (owner: Diego, due 2026-03-22). 3) Pilot with runtime-2.0 canary on 2026-04-01 using the new matrix. 4) Implement calendar automation and webhooks (owner: ENG SRE, estimate 3).

References and artifacts: Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Cross-Service+Release+Windowing, Google Drive doc (planning workbook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-release-workbook, Initial automation design doc: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/tree/demo, Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/release-health, Customer-facing status template: https://docs.redwood.ai/status-templates
